split/one: A single attention gives each token one blend of the others. But a word may need several things at once: say, the noun it describes, and the word just before it.
split/heads: Multi-head attention runs several attentions side by side. Each is a head, with its own query, key and value matrices, so each can look somewhere different.
split/width: The heads share the width. With d of five hundred twelve and h of eight heads, each head works in d over h dimensions: sixty four.
split/shapes: So one head's W Q is sixty four by five hundred twelve, its queries are T by sixty four, and its weights are T by T, as before.
join/concat: Each head outputs T by sixty four. Joined side by side, the eight make T by five hundred twelve again.
join/wo: One more matrix, W O, d by d, mixes what the heads found into one output per token.
join/count: Now count the weights. Eight heads' W Qs of sixty four by five hundred twelve hold as many as one d by d matrix. The same goes for W K and W V, and W O adds a fourth: four d squared.
join/same: That is exactly what a single head of full width would hold. Splitting into heads changes what attention can look for, not how many weights it has.
